Generate a synthetic bed

Source: R/generate.R
sw_generate.Rd

Shapes you can reason about, with optional fractal roughness on top. Local coordinates are metres from the grid centre, X east and Y north; row 1 is the north edge, as in a raster.

Usage

sw_generate(
  shape = names(.shapes),
  nx = 200,
  ny = nx,
  dx = 5,
  dy = dx,
  ...,
  noise = NULL,
  as = c("grid", "matrix")
)

Arguments

shape

one of the names above

nx, ny

cells across and down

dx, dy

cell size (m)

...

shape parameters, replacing the defaults (see `sw_shapes()`)

noise

NULL, or a list with `amp` (m) and optionally `scale`, `octaves`, `gain`, `seed` for [sw_fbm()]

as

"grid" for a grid in local metres with no CRS (a row-major vector with a `gis` attribute, as from `gdalraster::read_ds()`; plot it with `ximage::ximage()`, give it to [sw_from_rast()]) or "matrix" (with `dx`, `dy` attributes)

Details

* `plane`: `z0 - slope_x X - slope_y Y`. * `valley`: drains east, floor falling `slope`, sides rising `side` beyond a flat floor `floor` wide. * `bowl`: paraboloid, `depth` below rim level at the centre, rim at `radius`. * `shelf`: north-south coast at X = 0, land west rising `land_slope`, shelf east falling `shelf_slope` to `shelf_depth`, then `slope_slope` to `abyss`. * `island`: gaussian `height` above sea level on a floor `depth` deep. * `reservoir`: a valley with a dam at `dam_x`, `dam_height` above the floor there, `dam_thick` thick, breached over `breach` metres (0 = intact).
